title: 当AI全民"养智能体":顶级智能体 的真相,藏在"无需多言"的默契里
abstract: 摘要:当前AI行业掀起“养智能体”的宣传热潮,各大AI公司争相布局,却普遍存在对顶级智能体核心定义模糊的问题。本文结合行业现状,剖析普通智能体与顶级智能体的核心差距,提出顶级智能体的本质的是“精准捕捉意图、零额外输入产出”,并以“训练者仅发论文标题,智能体即可输出顶级论文”为具象场景,阐释接近顶级智能体的核心特征,反思行业宣传热潮背后的技术认知偏差,探讨AI智能体的发展方向与成熟标志。Abstract: Currently, the AI industry is experiencing an upsurge in promoting "raisingintelligent agents", with major AI companies scrambling to deploy them. However,there is a widespread ambiguity in the core definition of top-level intelligent agents.Combining the current industry situation, this paper analyzes the core gap betweenordinary intelligent agents and top-level intelligent agents, proposes that the essenceof top-level intelligent agents is "accurately capturing intentions and producingoutputs with zero additional input", and takes "trainers only sending a paper title andthe intelligent agent being able to output a top-level paper" as a specific scenario toexplain the core characteristics of approaching top-level intelligent agents. It reflectson the technical cognitive deviations behind the industry's promotion upsurge andexplores the development direction and maturity symbol of AI intelligent agents.

title: Multi-robot Three-Dimensional Path Planning Based on Multi-strategy Improved Dung Beetle Optimization Algorithm
abstract: To overcome the limitations of the original Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO) algorithm, such as weak global exploration ability, susceptibility to local optima, and low convergence accuracy, a multi-strategy improved DBO algorithm is proposed in this paper. The proposed method introduces a triangular walking strategy to improve the uniformity of global exploration, employs an iteration-based dynamic weight to guide the population toward promising regions, and adopts a Cauchy–Gaussian hybrid mutation strategy to balance global exploration and local exploitation. Six benchmark functions are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm. Experimental results show that the improved algorithm achieves better robustness and convergence accuracy compared with DBO, GWO, PSO, WOA, and HHO. Finally, the algorithm is applied to a robot path planning problem, demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority in solving practical engineering optimization problems. Furthermore, in the multi-robot path planning process, a dynamic target point—defined as the centroid of all robot positions at each iteration—is introduced to achieve the robot aggregation task. Finally, the proposed algorithm is applied to the multi-robot path planning problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving the aggregation task and its superiority in practical engineering optimization problems.

title: Ghost in the Agent: Redefining Information Flow Tracking for LLM Agents
abstract: Autonomous Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed to conduct complex tasks by interacting with external tools, APIs, and memory stores. However, processing untrusted external data exposes these agents to severe security threats, such as indirect prompt injection and unauthorized tool execution. Securing these systems requires effective information flow tracking. Yet, traditional taint analysis that is designed for program memory states fundamentally fails when applied to LLMs, where data propagation is governed by probabilistic natural language reasoning. In this paper, we present NeuroTaint, the first comprehensive taint tracking framework tailored for the unique information flow characteristics of LLM agents. Our key insight is that taint propagation in LLM agents must be understood not only as explicit content transfer, but also as semantic transformation, causal influence on decisions, and cross-session persistence through memory. NeuroTaint therefore audits execution traces offline to reconstruct provenance from untrusted sources to privileged sinks using semantic evidence, causal reasoning, and persistent context tracking, rather than relying on exact string matches or pre-defined source-sink paths alone. Extensive evaluation using TaintBench, our 400-scenario benchmark spanning 20 real-world agent frameworks, shows that NeuroTaint substantially outperforms FIDES, an information-flow-control (IFC)-style baseline for LLM agents, in source-sink propagation detection. We further show that NeuroTaint remains effective on established agent-security benchmarks, including InjecAgent and ToolEmu, while operating offline with modest additional auditing cost.

title: Lightweight and Production-Ready PDF Visual Element Parsing
abstract: PDF documents contain critical visual elements such as figures, tables, and forms whose accurate extraction is essential for document understanding and multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Existing PDF parsers often miss complex visuals, extract non-informative artifacts (e.g., watermarks, logos), produce fragmented elements, and fail to reliably associate captions with their corresponding elements, which degrades downstream retrieval and question answering. We present a lightweight and production level PDF parsing framework that can accurately detect visual elements and associates captions using a combination of spatial heuristics, layout analysis, and semantic similarity. On popular benchmark datasets and internal product data, the proposed solution achieves $\geq96\%$ visual element detection accuracy and $93\%$ caption association accuracy. When used as a preprocessing step for multimodal RAG, it significantly outperforms state-of-the-art parsers and large vision-language models on both internal data and the MMDocRAG benchmark, while reducing latency by over $2\times$. We have deployed the proposed system in challenging production environment.

title: Adaptive PID Control for Robotic Manipulators via Momentum-Based Actor-Critic Learning
abstract: This paper proposes the Momentum-enhanced Radial Basis Actor-Critic (MoRAC) algorithm, an online reinforcement learning framework for adaptive PID parameter optimization. By integrating momentum-based weight updates into a single RBF network, MoRAC addresses key limitations of conventional DRL-based controllers: it simplifies structural complexity, eliminates pre-training requirements, and suppresses parameter space oscillations. Simulations of trajectory tracking on a six-axis robotic manipulator demonstrate that MoRAC enhances computational efficiency by a factor of 2.64 compared to non-momentum baselines. Furthermore, comparative evaluations using IAE, MSE, and IATE metrics confirm that MoRAC significantly outperforms a PPO-optimized PID controller, delivering superior response speed and tracking accuracy in advanced control applications.

title: SemiGDA: Generative Dual-distribution Alignment for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Semi-supervised learning addresses label scarcity and high annotation costs in medical image segmentation by exploiting the latent information in unlabeled data to enhance model performance. Traditional discriminative segmentation relies on segmentation masks, neglecting feature-level distribution constraints. This limits robust semantic representation learning and adaptive modeling of unlabeled data in scenarios with few labels. To address these limitations, we propose SemiGDA, a novel Generative Dual-distribution Alignment framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Our SemiGDA overcomes the reliance of discriminative methods on large labeled datasets by aligning feature and semantic distributions to boost semantic learning and scene adaptability. Specifically, we propose a Dual-distribution Alignment Module (DAM), which employs two structurally distinct encoders to model image and mask feature distributions. It enforces their alignment in the latent space via distributional constraints, establishing structured feature consistency. Moreover, we design a Consistency-Driven Skip Adapter (CDSA) strategy, which introduces dual skip adapters (Image and Mask) to fuse multi-scale features via skip connections. Using a consistency loss, CDSA enhances cross-branch semantic alignment and reinforces fine-grained semantic consistency. Experimental results on diverse medical datasets show that our method outperforms other state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods. Code is released at: https://github.com/taozh2017/SemiGDA.

title: The Necessity and Methodological Foundations of Using Artificial Intelligence Technologies in The Professional Training of Future Physical Education Teachers
abstract: This article analyzes the relevance, necessity, and methodological foundations of using artificial intelligence technologies in improving the professional training of future physical education teachers. In the digital educational environment, the possibilities of artificial intelligence for individualizing the learning process, monitoring, analyzing, and forecasting educational outcomes are scientifically substantiated. The paper also highlights ways to enhance the effectiveness of education through the application of modern technologies in physical education classes.

title: HAR-CRO: Hybrid Adaptive Resonance Chrono-Optimization for Deterministic Global Convergence in Non-Convex Landscapes
abstract: High-dimensional non-convex optimization remains a fundamental bottleneck in modern machine learning, where traditional methods fail to guarantee deterministic global convergence. We introduce HAR-CRO: Hybrid Adaptive Resonance Chrono-Optimization, a novel optimizer achieving deterministic global convergence in non-convex landscapes through two mechanisms: Temporal Adaptive Resonance and Commutative Logic. HAR-CRO resolves Hessian singularity, guarantees finite oscillations, and outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms with precision up to 1e-16. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate >100x improvement in accuracy and convergence speed. Code and simulator are ready for industrial deployment.

title: Clause AI-7: Structural Coherence Bound — Dirichlet Energy Band Specification for MAI-1 Invariant 4
abstract: Formal derivation of MAI-1 Invariant 4, the Structural Coherence Bound. This specification provides the complete mathematical foundation for continuous monitoring of representational health in deployed foundation models via Dirichlet energy band certification. The document defines the spectral graph-theoretic formulation of Dirichlet energy adapted to transformer architectures through the attention-as-dynamic-graph construction. It formally characterizes two failure modes that coherence monitoring detects: representational collapse, where internal features collapse to a low-dimensional subspace incapable of distinguishing meaningfully different inputs, linked to oversmoothing, neural collapse, dimensional collapse, token uniformity, and loss of plasticity; and representational fragmentation, where representations fragment into chaotically sensitive manifolds exploitable by adversarial perturbation, linked to oversquashing, over-sharpening, chaotic dynamics, and adversarial vulnerability. The specification includes the effective rank complementary diagnostic for capturing representational degradation in subspaces orthogonal to graph structure, the layer-wise measurement methodology with attention-weighted energy computation and head aggregation, the efficient inference-time computation architecture achieving coherence monitoring within a less than 2% latency budget via Top-K sparsification, stochastic trace estimation, randomized SVD, and Frobenius proxy metrics, the calibration procedure for establishing the certified coherence band from validation data with conformal coverage guarantees, and the compliance state machine with deterministic transition rules. With Clause AI-7 enforced alongside AI-8 (Entropy Collapse Constraint), AI-2 (Gradient Starvation Envelope), AI-6 (Distribution Drift Bound), and AI-4 (SRAM Thermal Integrity Bound), all five mandatory MAI-1 invariants are formally derived with full calibration methodology, completing the analytical core of the Auburn Governance Stack's Layer 2 invariant suite. This work was previously hosted on Figshare, where the author maintained a portfolio of 29 publications with minted DOIs and an established ORCID record. The author's Figshare account was disabled without prior notice, without citation of a specific terms violation, and without opportunity for review, rendering all published items and their associated DOIs inaccessible. No communication was provided before or at the time of the disable action. This deposit and associated deposits on Zenodo ensure continued public accessibility of the author's research on institutional infrastructure with appropriate permanence guarantees

title: Rapid Knowledge Transformation Method for Highway Engineering Survey and Design Data Based on Large Language Models
abstract: This paper introduces a rapid knowledge transformation approach leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to address the critical challenges of low knowledge utilization and slow retrieval responses stemming from massive unstructured data in highway engineering survey and design. The methodology is executed in three progressive stages. Initially, unstructured data undergoes information extraction and structural processing to convert it into LLM-friendly formats. Subsequently, a specialized highway domain ontology is developed to provide a semantic framework; this guides the LLM in deep semantic understanding and information extraction, thereby automating the construction of a high-fidelity knowledge graph (KG). Building upon this structured foundation, an innovative hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture is developed, seamlessly integrating the KG with vector databases. Furthermore, this study establishes the industry's first benchmark for evaluating the knowledge-processing workflow of highway engineering data. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline method of directly inputting raw data, the proposed hybrid approach effectively mitigates context loss during long-document retrieval and accelerates response speeds by at least 50%. evidence.title: Rapid Knowledge Transformation Method for Highway Engineering Survey and Design Data Based on Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: This paper introduces a rapid knowledge transformation approach leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to address the critical challenges of low knowledge utilization and slow retrieval responses stemming from massive unstructured data in highway engineering survey and design. The methodology is executed in three progressive stages. Initially, unstructured data undergoes information extraction and structural processing to convert it into LLM-friendly formats. Subsequently, a specialized highway domain ontology is developed to provide a semantic framework; this guides the LLM in deep semantic understanding and information extraction, thereby automating the construction of a high-fidelity knowledge graph (KG). Building upon this structured foundation, an innovative hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture is developed, seamlessly integrating the KG with vector databases. Furthermore, this study establishes the industry's first benchmark for evaluating the knowledge-processing workflow of highway engineering data. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to the baseline method of directly inputting raw data, the proposed hybrid approach effectively mitigates context loss during long-document retrieval and accelerates response speeds by at least 50%. Real-world engineering applications validate that this solution significantly empowers intelligent knowledge management in the highway survey and design sector.

title: A Hierarchical Ensemble Inference Pipeline for Robust White Blood Cell Classification Under Domain Shifts
abstract: Automated white blood cell (WBC) classification is essential for scalable leukaemia screening. However, real-world deployment is challenged by domain shifts caused by staining protocols, scanner characteristics, and inter-laboratory variability, which often degrade model performance. The White Blood Cell Classification Challenge (WBCBench) at ISBI 2026 aims to advance robust WBC recognition, with a focus on accurately identifying blast cells and other clinically critical rare subtypes. We propose a memory-augmented, hierarchical ensemble pipeline for WBC classification under domain shifts, leveraging a feature bank and a DinoBloom backbone fine-tuned with LoRA. Our three-stage inference hierarchy combines k-nearest neighbors (kNN) retrieval at each level, reducing over-reliance on any single decision. Evaluated on the WBCBench dataset, our method ranks within the top ten by macro F1-score in the final testing phase.

title: A model construction of personalized teaching of English writing based on reinforcement learning
abstract: By constructing a deep knowledge tracking model based on reinforcement learning theory, students can choose more suitable courses or exercises when selecting learning resources. In view of this, the article proposes a temporal convolutional knowledge tracking model (TCKT-FI) based on reinforcement learning, which obtains students' knowledge mastery state through temporal convolutional network, solves the long sequence dependency problem by using causal convolution and inflationary convolution, and solves the gradient vanishing and exploding problems by using residual network to deal with the deep network structure. Following that, a recommendation algorithm framework based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRR) is proposed, and better recommendation strategies (Actor) and value functions (Critic) are explored. Finally, the model's English writing knowledge tracking effect is tested and its performance is verified through experiments. The knowledge tracking effect test experiment shows that at moments 1.1~5, 5.8-9.5, 10.5-15, when students did not learn the knowledge point, the TCKT-FI model shows a significant downward trend, indicating that students have forgotten the knowledge point, but the comparison model fails to simulate the forgetting process of students well. This confirms the accuracy of the model and the efficiency of its calculation. It has practical value in the personalized teaching of English writing.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for Heart Disease Prediction
abstract: Abstract This research focuses on building an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) system that helps make machine learning–based heart disease prediction more transparent and trustworthy for medical professionals. Although modern AI models can achieve impressive accuracy in healthcare, many of them operate as “black boxes,” making it difficult for clinicians to understand why a particular prediction is made. This lack of clarity often limits their acceptance and use in real clinical settings. To bridge this gap, the study presents a web-based diagnostic platform that combines powerful machine learning models—such as Random Forest and XGBoost—with well-established explainability techniques, namely SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations). The models are trained using the widely used UCI Heart Disease Dataset, which includes important clinical features like age, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and chest pain type. The platform is designed to give doctors clear, real-time explanations for every prediction. It allows them to see not only how the model behaves overall but also why it produced a specific result for an individual patient. Through an intuitive Streamlit-based interface, clinicians can enter patient details, view heart disease risk predictions, and explore interactive visualizations such as SHAP summary plots, feature dependency graphs, and LIME-based local explanations. In addition to measuring standard performance metrics like accuracy, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, the system is evaluated for its practical usefulness and interpretability through simulated clinical cases and feedback from healthcare professionals. Early testing shows that adding explainability significantly improves transparency, builds clinician confidence, and supports better-informed medical decision-making. Overall, the study highlights that explainability is not just an optional feature but a critical requirement for the responsible and effective use of AI in sensitive medical applications. Future improvements could include extending the system to predict multiple diseases, integrating it with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), supporting mobile health platforms, and deploying it on the cloud to enable scalable and collaborative clinical use. Keywords: Explainable AI (XAI), Heart Disease Prediction, SHAP, LIME, Interpretable Machine Learning, Clinical Decision Support, Healthcare Transparency, Model Explainability, Random Forest.

title: AI-Powered Personalized Learning and Career Enhancement Platform
abstract: Choosing a suitable career has become increasing obstacle for students in higher secondary and undergraduate programs. Many students find it difficult to identify career paths that align with their interests, psychological traits, and skill levels. Traditional career counselling app methods typically depend on static questionnaires and general recommendations, which often fail to address individual uniqueness. This study proposes an AI-powered personalized learning and career enhancement platform that combines psychological assessment, career recommendation, and adaptive course generation. The system leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide intelligent and context-aware guidance. Users are tested through dynamically generated psychological questions designed to identify personality traits and career inclinations across multiple dimensions. Based on the psychological profile and skill-level assessment, the system recommends suitable career paths and generates a customized learning roadmap. Developed using Python and Django, the platform ensures continuous interaction between reasoning models and knowledge retrieval mechanisms. The proposed solution Aims to improve career clarity and learning efficiency through end-to-end personalization.

title: Campus AI Assistant Chatbot
abstract: This project presents an AI-powered college assistant designed to provide instant and accurate information about various aspects of an institution, including departments, faculty, placements, and facilities. The system uses a combination of data retrieval techniques and a language model to understand user queries and respond in a conversational manner. By integrating college-specific data, it ensures relevant and reliable answers. The solution reduces the need for manual enquiry, improves accessibility, and enhances user experience. It is lightweight, cost-effective, and can be easily adapted by other institutions to create a smarter and more efficient information system.

title: CREDIT CARD FRAUD DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING
authors: International Journal for Research In Science & Advanced Technologies
abstract: In Credit card fraud detection is presently the most frequently occurring problem in the present world. This is due to the rise in both online transactions and e-commerce platforms. Credit card fraud generally happens when the card was stolen for any of the unauthorized purposes or even when the fraudster uses the credit card information for his use. In the present world, we are facing a lot of credit card problems. To detect the fraudulent activities the credit card fraud detection system was introduced. This project aims to focus mainly on machine learning algorithms. The algorithms used are random forest algorithm and the Adaboost algorithm. The results of the two algorithms are based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The ROC curve is plotted based on the confusion matrix. The Random Forest and the Adaboost algorithms are compared and the algorithm that has the greatest accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score is considered as the best algorithm that is used to detect the fraud.
